title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ‘Resilience, Inclusiveness, Stability and Empowerment of Communities (RISE-K)’ project in Moroto, Amudat and Nakapiripirit districts of Karamoja sub-region in Uganda, implemented by Oxfam through ICSP will directly reach 37,970 women, youth and other vulnerable people from mining and pastoralist communities who are living under extreme poverty and facing severe labour rights violations. Oxfam will partner with Resource Rights Africa, Centre for Budget and Tax Policy, National Association of Women of Uganda (NAWOU), Uganda Women Network (UWONET), CARITAS Moroto, TUNADO and Land Justice Network to deliver interventions focusing on governance and accountability for effective service delivery, promotion of women’s rights, enhanced local capacity for effective people-centered, climate and conflict -sensitive, gender-responsive and inclusive disaster preparedness and response and improved income and food security. This project outcome in addition to promoting sustainable livelihoods is also intended to restore, rehabilitate, and protect the water catchment areas in targeted communities experiencing prolonged periods of drought as a result of climate change. This is a critical intervention under this impact area of the programme and would have not been funded if this intervention was not implemented.
